statement: For the block matrix M = [[A, B], [C, D]] with A invertible, eliminating x from the linear system M[x;y] = [u;v] produces a reduced equation in y alone whose coefficient matrix is the Schur complement of A in M: S := D - C A^{-1} B.

symbols.meaning: p x p block of M, assumed invertible for this elimination

Schur complement of A in M

steps.text: Write the block system [[A,B],[C,D]][x;y] = [u;v] as two separate equations: Ax + By = u, and Cx + Dy = v.
Solve the first equation for x, using invertibility of A: x = A^{-1}(u - By).

Substitute this expression for x into the second equation: C A^{-1}(u - By) + Dy = v, which rearranges to (D - C A^{-1} B) y = v - C A^{-1} u. This is the reduced equation, and its coefficient matrix defines the Schur complement of A in M: S := D - C A^{-1} B.
Solve the reduced equation for y: y = S^{-1}(v - C A^{-1} u).
Substitute this y back into the expression for x from step 2 to eliminate y: x = (A^{-1} + A^{-1} B S^{-1} C A^{-1}) u - A^{-1} B S^{-1} v.

Collect the two solutions into matrix form, [x;y] = [[A^{-1}+A^{-1}BS^{-1}CA^{-1}, -A^{-1}BS^{-1}], [-S^{-1}CA^{-1}, S^{-1}]] [u;v], which is exactly M^{-1}. Comparing the (2,2) block shows S^{-1} equals the (2,2) block entry of M^{-1}, i.e. the Schur complement is the inverse of the (2,2) block entry of M^{-1}.

assumptions.breaks_when: A is singular, so step 2's elimination x = A^{-1}(u - By) is undefined.
A is ill-conditioned, in which case the source notes the elimination algorithm is not numerically accurate even though it remains algebraically valid.

failure_modes.mode: Reduced equation has no unique solution for y.
failure_modes.signature: S = D - C A^{-1} B is singular.
failure_modes.cause: The Schur complement itself is not invertible, even though A is invertible, so step 4 cannot be carried out.
A is singular, so x cannot be solved for and eliminated in step 2.
